skill.name: invoking-agents
skill.description: Coordinates one issue through separate implementation, review, QA, risk classification, pull request creation, escalation, and cleanup processes.
skill.summary: Orchestrate issue delivery across separate implementation, review, and QA agents.
skill.author: drix10

security_audit.summary: The 81 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, safe documentation references, or fixed workflow checks. Two semantic risks remain: unconfined implementer processes and unsafe shell interpolation of an untrusted issue title.

remediation.issue: Claude and Codex implementers are not technically confined to the issue worktree.
remediation.suggestion: Require a container or enforced sandbox for implementers, restrict writable paths to the worktree, and stop when confinement is unavailable.

remediation.issue: The pull request command interpolates an untrusted issue title into shell text.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the title as a separately quoted process argument or create the pull request through a structured API without shell interpolation.

semantic_findings.title: Unconfined Implementer Processes
semantic_findings.description: Claude and Codex implementers run without enforced worktree confinement while processing untrusted issue content. Environment variables and prompts are advisory, so a compromised agent could modify files outside the worktree.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly states that Claude and Codex lack worktree confinement and recommends an external container or sandbox. Their launch commands do not enforce that boundary.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Issue Title Interpolated Into Shell Command
semantic_findings.description: The pull request command places the untrusted issue title inside a double-quoted shell argument. Shell substitutions within a title could execute unless the value is escaped or passed without shell parsing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill declares issue text untrusted, then shows the issue title substituted into a shell command. Double quotes do not suppress shell command substitution.

content.user_title: Orchestrate Issues Through Review and QA
content.value_statement: Multi-agent issue delivery can lose state, mix roles, and skip safeguards. This skill coordinates implementation, review, QA, escalation, and pull request creation through agent-flow.
actual_capabilities: Loads an issue from user input, GitHub, or local issue files.
Creates an issue worktree and tracks workflow state through agent-flow.
Runs separate implementer, reviewer, and QA processes with artifact handoffs.
Classifies changed files and escalates protected or critical changes.
Creates a pull request after review and QA requirements pass.
limitations: Requires agent-flow commands and compatible agent command-line tools.
GitHub issue and pull request steps require gh authentication and network access.
Claude and Codex implementers need external sandboxing for enforced worktree confinement.
Ambiguous specifications, architecture decisions, and repeated failures require human action.

use_cases.title: Deliver a GitHub Issue
use_cases.description: Run one tracked issue through implementation, independent review, QA, and pull request creation.

use_cases.title: Process a Local Work Item
use_cases.description: Use acceptance criteria from local issue files when a GitHub issue is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Enforce Review Separation
use_cases.description: Keep implementation, review, and QA in separate processes with file-based evidence and bounded review rounds.

prompt_templates.title: Run One Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement issue #{issue_number} through the full agent-flow pipeline and open a pull request.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for an existing GitHub issue.

prompt_templates.title: Use Local Acceptance Criteria
prompt_templates.prompt: Process the work item in {issue_file} as issue {issue_number}, then implement, review, test, and prepare a pull request.
prompt_templates.scenario: Workflow for a repository without an accessible GitHub issue.

prompt_templates.title: Resume an Escalated Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume issue #{issue_number} after this decision: {decision}. Preserve existing artifacts and continue from the recorded state.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify issues {issue_numbers}, identify overlapping files, run independent worktrees in parallel, and serialize any conflicting changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for multiple independent tasks.

output_examples.input: Implement issue #42 and open a pull request.
output_examples.output: Issue #42 completed. Implementation, review, and QA passed. Pull request #108 was opened from the issue branch.
Issue #57 needs a human decision because the acceptance criteria conflict. The decision brief includes the exact ambiguity and attempted resolution.

output: Issue #60 started in its own worktree.
Issue #61 was serialized because both classifications include the same file.

best_practices: Provide testable acceptance criteria before starting the pipeline.
Use enforced containers or sandboxes for every agent that can edit or execute commands.
Review escalation briefs and critical draft pull requests before continuing.
anti_patterns: Do not combine implementer, reviewer, and QA responsibilities in one agent context.
Do not bypass protected-path checks, review-round limits, or required human approval.
Do not interpolate issue text directly into shell commands.

faq.question: Which issue sources are supported?
faq.answer: The skill accepts inline criteria, GitHub issues through gh, and local ISSUES.md or .agent-issues.json files.

faq.question: Does it implement changes itself?
faq.answer: No. It coordinates separate implementer, reviewer, and QA processes and exchanges artifacts between them.

faq.question: When does it request human input?
faq.answer: It escalates missing specifications, architecture decisions, protected-path changes, critical changes, repeated failures, and unavailable GitHub operations.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It pushes the issue branch and uses gh after implementation, review, and QA complete.

faq.question: Does it support parallel issues?
faq.answer: Yes. Independent issues can use separate worktrees, but issues touching the same files should run sequentially.

faq.question: Is worktree confinement automatic?
faq.answer: Only some harnesses enforce it. Claude and Codex implementers require an external container or sandbox for a hard boundary.
